title.narrative: Providing sustainable and lifesaving WASH services to climate change-affected rural and displaced populations in Qansax-dhere district, Bay region.

description.narrative: ltpgtAMARD proposes a 8-month WASH project aimed at providing lifesaving and sustainable services to drought- and conflict-affected communities in Qansaxdhere district. The project targets 12, 780 people 10, 280 displaced and 2,500 rural population, with a special focus on female-headed households, pregnant and lactating women, children under five, persons with disabilities and individuals from minority communities who continue to face exclusion, and limited access to safe water and sanitation, increasing their risk of disease and displacement. The project objective is to improve access to safe water and sanitation, reduce the incidence of waterborne diseases, and prevent further displacement by strengthening the resilience of crisis-affected populations. To achieve this, AMARD will rehabilitate and construct 5 communal water sources in 5 rural villages Buula Qumaar, Weyl Malssh , Buula mundulla, Ceel baraf, Ceel adaad to improve access to safe water. 3 of the shallow wells in Qumaar, Weyl Malssh and Ceel Baraf will be fully solarized to ensure uninterrupted water supply for both host and rural communities while 2 shallow communal wells serving host communities in Bulla mundulla and Ceel Adad will be rehabilitated and installed with hand pump for protection. The shallow wells will benefit 2500 rural communities. 25 WASH committees selected from the targeted villages will be trained. The project conducted targeted chlorination of 6 communal water sources which will be identified through risk assessment jointly conducted with the state ministry of water and other WASH partners. 65 emergency latrines will be built in IDP sites and institutions this will include 60 latrines for IDPs Buusley, Babado,Tirka, Hareeri jiroon, Xafata, and Lowforar IDP camps. 5 for Wazarada hospital and 10 disability friendly latrines in the same IDP sites. the latrines will improve access to sanitation for 2,250 people. Sanitation tools will be distributed to hygiene promoters and WASH committees. The project will distribute 1,500 Hygiene to vulnerable households at high risk of AWD/Cholera,.10 hygiene promoters will be trained to support sustained hygiene behavior change through structured campaigns and environmental clean-up activities. Access to sanitation will be improved at health and nutrition facilities to ensure continuity of service delivery. Protection will be mainstreamed by integrating safety measures and community engagement strategies to ensure equitable access to water and sanitation services for all, particularly vulnerable populations in IDP sites and rural villages. Community engagement will be prioritized to ensure accountability, reduce exclusion, mitigate protection risks and aid diversion. The project has a robust CFM mechanism and hotlines. The project is delivered in close coordination with nutrition, health, CCCM, and protection partners to maximize impact and ensure a well-integrated response. Referral pathways will be strengthened to link malnourished children to nutrition and health services. Behavior change campaigns will promote handwashing, safe water use, menstrual hygiene, and other practices critical to reducing malnutrition and WASH-related diseases. AMARD is a local, Minority rights-based organization with an active presence in Qansaxdhere district. As an active WASH, Protection, and CCCM partner, AMARD has demonstrated the ability to implement WASH projects in hard-to-reach areas. With deep community trust, AMARD will leverage its operational presence to deliver the project. AMARD is currently implementing emergency WASH activities targeting 4 IDP settlement in Qansaxdhere. SHF funding will compliment this emergency WASH activities giving AMARD the capacity to expand geographically and ensure continuity of service.
